Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for acute left-sided headache with visual disturbance, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting; clinical impression of migraine; advised OTC therapy (ibuprofen + antiemetic) and sugary beverage; arranged same-day in-person assessment for neurological exam with option to cancel if markedly improved.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache with visual changes.
- Onset/duration: Began this morning; symptoms present for ~4 hours at time of consult.
- Character/progression: Sudden onset; unilateral (left-sided), described as severe; pain intensity 5–6/10 (10 = prior kidney stone pain). Worsens with movement; prefers keeping head still.
- Location: Left side of head; not clearly behind the eye.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Visual disturbance: Blurred vision with zigzag lines; cannot tolerate screens.
  - Dizziness.
  - Nausea; vomiting x2 starting at onset; ongoing nausea.
  - Denies limb weakness; walking reported as normal.
- Prior episodes: No previous headaches like this.
- Medications tried: Paracetamol taken ~3 hours after onset (i.e., ~1 hour into headache); no relief.
- Pregnancy: Patient feels pregnancy is unlikely.
- Concerns: Worried about serious causes (tumor, stroke).
- Systems review (pertinent negatives/positives as documented): No focal weakness; gait normal. No other neurological deficits reported.

Past Medical History:
- Kidney stones (prior history; no details on timing/management).

Medications:
- Current/Recent:
  - Paracetamol taken once; ineffective (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Regular medications: None reported.
- Plan/Recommendations:
  - Ibuprofen recommended (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Antiemetic from pharmacy recommended (agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Sugary carbonated drink (e.g., cola) recommended.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Pregnancy considered unlikely by patient.
- Tobacco, alcohol, recreational drug use: not discussed.
- Other social factors: not discussed.

Family History:
- Mother: Migraines.
- Mother: Hypothyroidism. (Conflict noted: clinician referenced “hyperthyroid” before patient clarified hypothyroidism.)

Physical Examination:
- 

Investigations:
- None performed/reported.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache with visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting — likely migraine.
  - Assessment: First episode of this type; unilateral pain, visual zigzag lines, nausea/vomiting consistent with migraine. No focal deficits reported; gait normal. Paracetamol ineffective.
  - Plan:
    - Trial ibuprofen plus an anti-sickness medication available from pharmacy.
    - Drink a sugary, carbonated beverage (e.g., cola).
    - Arrange same-day in-person evaluation for full neurological examination.
    - If symptoms markedly improve before the appointment, patient may cancel by calling the clinic.
    - If any further problems occur before the appointment, contact the clinic.
- Issue 2: Patient anxiety regarding serious pathology (tumor/stroke).
  - Assessment: Features more suggestive of migraine; reassurance provided.
  - Plan: Proceed with above management and in-person neurologic exam to further assess; return/notify if worsening or new concerns arise.

General Plan items:
- Consider escalation to specific migraine-relief medication if initial measures are ineffective (to be addressed at in-person assessment).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals not recorded.
  - No physical/neurological exam performed (telemedicine).
  - No documentation of photophobia, phonophobia, neck stiffness, fever, recent head trauma, or infection symptoms beyond what is stated.
  - No medication doses/routes/frequencies documented for paracetamol, ibuprofen, or antiemetic.
  - Smoking, alcohol, and substance use not assessed.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Family history thyroid disorder: clinician said “hyperthyroid,” patient clarified “hypothyroidism” (conflict noted; patient report used).
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor connectivity issues; otherwise intelligible.
